newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S'pore jet fuel depressed on lack of Japan buying.
newsitem.headline: S'pore jet fuel depressed on lack of Japan buying.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel prices are low, relative to soaring gas oil prices, as big buyers in Japan continued to stay away despite the approaching winter demand period, industry sources said on Thursday.
The absence of Japanese buying has already led to a big drop in Middle East premiums from 80 cents to 5-10 cents a barrel in three weeks, traders said.
This week, a 30,000-tonne dual purpose kerosene cargo for October lifting was sold at 5-10 cents premium to prevailing Middle East quotes, traders said.
"Gulf producers are still in jet producing mode and there are cargoes available for lifting in late October," one trader said.
Premiums in Singapore have slipped to about 10 cents above spot quotes against 30 cents in early September.
Spot prices in Singapore hovered around $30.00 per barrel over the past few weeks, despite a $2-3 gain to gas oil prices.

Japan is staying out of the market as it had steadily built up its stocks during the off-season summer months and end-August inventories grew 36.9 percent from a month earlier to 4.18 million kilolitres (kl)--up sharply from the record low of 2.65 million kl in January.
Stocks in September are expected to be higher than August at around 4.47 million kl, the same volumes as September 1995.
A trader in a Japanese trading house said imports should remain high for September but are not expected to be as much for October and November arrivals.

Traders said it is now even economical to export Middle East jet fuel cargoes to Europe, but to make it profitable players need to secure very competitive freight rates and have a ready market in the west.
Unlike gas oil, which has been sold extensively from the Middle East to the Meditterenean, jet fuel has to overcome an additional six-percent import tax that is imposed by Europe.
A source said one Red Sea cargo of jet fuel was sold recently for export to Northwest Europe.
"The Gulf producers will switch away from jet mode if the jet/gas oil spread on paper falls below $1.00," one trader said.
The physical jet fuel/gas oil spread is at about 50 cents but the October swaps is quoted at $1.00/1.40 while November is wider at $1.80/2.10.
Jet fuel/gas oil swap spread is not likely to turn negative, that is for gas oil to cost more than jet fuel, traders said.
Refiners would be quick to adjust their production before jet fuel values dip below gas oil as they would be looking at the swaps markets to determine output slates, a refiner said.
Traders said in the near future the market could improve if India buys more than the five cargoes it bought in October in its monthly tender. India's November tender closes on Thursday.
Looking ahead, traders said Japan should enter the market to buy jet-kerosene fuel from the Middle East and Singapore for lifting in November for arrival in December.
"I think the market has bottomed. We are hearing some buying interest for November barrels," one trader said.
Also prices should firm as the 305,000-barrel-per-day Jubail refinery in Saudi Arabia is due for a 30-day maintenance beginning in November, he said.
But stocks in Asia remain high with one trader said to have up to two million barrels in storage in Guam and also unsold cargoes on board vessels bound for this region, traders said.
--Singapore Newsroom (+65-870-3093)
